findings.where: agent_loop.py:524 (output = stdout + stderr), agent_loop.py:224-230 (last inject_auroc line wins), agent_loop.py:541/723 (returncode never checked); val_bpb_parse.py:55
findings.scenario: train.py prints 'inject_auroc: 0.99' to stderr (concatenated after the scorer's stdout so it is the final match), or prints it and os._exit()s before eval/objective.py scores anything. Same for val_bpb in the default objective: train.py prints its own 'val_bpb:' line. Non-zero exit and timeouts are not treated as failures.
findings.reproducer: repro_forge.py: stderr forgery parsed as 0.999 (rc=0); exit-before-scorer parsed as 0.99 with rc=1
findings.inflates: which commits the loop keeps; any 'kept for inject_auroc/val_bpb' number. Held-out HDFS re-evaluation (eval/agent_commits.py) re-measures, so final real-data AUROC is not directly forged by this path.

findings.where: eval/objective.py:76-91 (exec train.py in-process; model/tokenizer taken from its namespace) and :51-52 (eval.in_domain/eval.inject imported AFTER exec)
findings.scenario: train.py rebinds eval.in_domain.token_surprise/model_scores_for, prepare.get_token_bytes/MAX_SEQ_LEN, torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy, or sets `model`/`tokenizer` to arbitrary objects; it can also read AOMB_OBJECTIVE_VAL to learn the exact clean texts.
findings.reproducer: repro_monkeypatch.py: with no model at all, patched scorer yields inject_auroc 1.0 on every corruption
findings.inflates: inject_auroc used for keep decisions. The docstring already says 'not a sandbox'; the risk is adversarial or accidental (e.g. a global torch patch).

findings.scenario: The 300 clean sessions the objective scores are the first rows of hdfs_sessions.val.jsonl, which is also the pinned val shard. train.py controls its dataloader and can train on split='val' (a one-line, innocent-looking 'more data' change). The model then memorises exactly the clean sessions, so corrupted copies look more surprising -> inject_auroc rises AND val_bpb falls, with no real gain. Nothing in the loop detects it.
findings.inflates: inject_auroc and val_bpb keep decisions. Real HDFS eval split is disjoint (checked), so agent_commits would expose it. Recommend grepping the kept train.py patches for '"val"', AOMB_OBJECTIVE, sys.modules, 'eval.' imports, monkeypatching.

findings.where: eval/select_rule.py:29-36 (VIEWS include HDFS 'all' eval rows); scripts/agent_inject_experiment.sh:150-152 (--primary bpb_top10 on the same HDFS eval split)
findings.scenario: The 'pre-registered' bpb_top10 rule was chosen by mean AUROC over six views that include the full labelled HDFS eval set; the agent's 'held-out real HDFS AUROC' is then measured with that rule on the same 10k HDFS eval blocks. The rule is not held out from HDFS. BGL is not among the views (selection code never reads it), but loghub_bgl.py (a7cba47, 2026-10-09 18:19) was committed 11 min before select_rule.py (1f77d4a, 18:30), so code dates cannot prove BGL results were unseen at selection.
findings.inflates: absolute fixed-rule AUROC on HDFS (base vs agent deltas less affected since both use the same rule). BGL is the only clean test of the rule.

findings.where: agent_loop.py:741 (keep = beats best-so-far + MIN_DELTA); scripts/agent_inject_experiment.sh:93-103 (MIN_DELTA = max(0.005, 2*pstdev of 3 base runs)); train.py:594 (fixed torch seed 42)
findings.scenario: ~120 noisy trials against a running max with a margin from n=3 base runs (population sd) -> winner's-curse: the reported best inject_auroc/val_bpb is biased upward, and some keeps can be noise. Seed is fixed, so 'repeat' runs in agent_commits (--repeat-ends) sample only MPS nondeterminism, not seed variance; base-vs-final real AUROC differences get no seed-level CI.
findings.inflates: best-so-far objective values; significance of base->final real-HDFS AUROC change.

findings.where: prepare.py:379 (logits = model(x)), train.py:146-152 (attention mask is agent-editable)
findings.scenario: evaluate_bpb correctly computes plain CE from logits (verified, tests/test_evaluate_bpb_integrity.py guards the loss-path bypass), but the forward pass is agent code: a non-causal mask (is_causal=False / wrong triu) leaks the target token into x, and train.py may also call evaluate_bpb with anything or skip it and print a number (finding 1). No test checks causality or that train.py's printed val_bpb came from prepare.evaluate_bpb.

The prompt discloses the exact scoring rule (top-10% bits) and the 7 corruption types, and the corruption set was designed after HDFS results existed (eval/inject.py first commit a7cba47 2026-10-09; HDFS ingest 2026-09-27). Truncation/missing-event corruptions mirror HDFS's known anomaly types, and the inject-vs-real correlation was validated on HDFS, the same dataset used for the agent's real check.
findings.inflates: generalisation claims of the injected-fault objective beyond HDFS.

findings.scenario: Fault-control traffic is captured as telemetry: 'fault_mode_set_mode=latency|errors|both' logs and 'op=POST_/admin/fault' spans land in incident-labelled sessions (and 'mode=none' in normals). strip_meta_lines removes only '# aomb_meta' lines. Also 'induced_fault_error' text in 51 incident error logs (a real error message, but names the injection).
findings.reproducer: check_lab2.py: 8 incident-labelled sessions in pooled-20260918 carry the fault name via the admin call (of 1444 incidents)

findings.scenario: Orphan logs (no trace_id) are grouped into sessions BY window label, so session membership is defined by the label. In published captures this yields one 1-line normal session, so no measurable effect, but any capture with orphan logs would get one giant per-label session.

Model variants returning NaN (bpb_max_event with no line >=8 bytes, bits_max_field with no field) are scored on a smaller subset than baselines; if NaN sessions are hard cases the model's AUROC is computed without them. 'n' is recorded, so it is detectable.
findings.inflates: model-variant AUROC where NaNs occur (likely rare on HDFS/lab).

findings.scenario: spearman() ranks without tie averaging, so tied val_bpb/AUROC values are ranked by input order (x=[1,1,1,2], y=[1,2,3,4] gives 1.0; tie-aware value 0.775).
findings.inflates: the reported val_bpb vs AUROC rank correlation when ties exist.

findings.scenario: In the lab and RCAEval every incident is later in time than every eval normal (lab: 0/3531 incidents precede the end of their capture's train normals). A time-drift detector would get credit. Placebo (fit baselines on earliest normals, rank later normals vs earlier normals) gives baselines ~0.50 everywhere (lab duration_z 0.52-0.56), so drift is small for baselines; the LM was not placebo-tested (needs training).
findings.inflates: possibly model AUROC on lab/RCAEval; recommend a model placebo run.

findings.scenario: On HDFS/BGL msg values are joined with '_', so value_* baselines, bits_max_field and the value_swap/value_cross injections see only the first word of msg. Not crippling (novelty/sequence_novelty use full templates) but value baselines are weak on log datasets by construction; error_lines/rule are all-zero on HDFS (no ERROR/FATAL lines), AUROC 0.5 by ties.

clean_checks: HDFS split: train/eval/val session ids pairwise disjoint; train all normal; eval first-appearance strictly after last train block; val drawn after the train window, excluded from train+eval (loghub_hdfs.py:71-109, check_hdfs.py)
HDFS: 0/271 eval incidents are exact (ts-masked) duplicates of a train session; 118/9729 eval normals and 10/1000 val are (natural repetition, not contamination)
No label text in HDFS sessions (only level/svc/msg fields; label column dropped); BGL drops the label column (loghub_bgl.py:59)
Tokenizer for the agent runs is trained on train shards only (prepare.py:136-138 excludes the val shard); fixture tokenizer fit on train_texts only (fixture_train.py)
sessions_to_shards refuses incident text in train or val shards (sessions_to_shards.py:34-35); objective value pool uses split=='train' rows only
Injected-fault clean set (val file) is disjoint from the HDFS eval split used for the real-detection check
All baselines (duration stats, novelty sets, ValueStats, min_lines, Injector pool) are fit on train normals only (in_domain.py:528-531, 550)
# aomb_meta lines stripped before scoring and before baselines (labels.py:77-87, 116)
auroc/pr_auc match sklearn roc_auc_score/average_precision_score to 1e-16 on 300 random tie-heavy cases; ties -> 0.5; one class -> NaN; direction higher=anomalous
Seeds aggregated as mean/std of per-seed AUROC (in_domain.py:636-645), not max
prepare.evaluate_bpb computes plain CE from model(x) logits; test guards against the targets/reduction path
Sliding-window attention mask in current train.py is causal (tril then triu)
NaN/inf val_bpb or inject_auroc are rejected and rolled back (val_bpb_parse.py:24-38, regex excludes 'nan')
Temporal placebo for baselines on RCAEval OB/TT and three lab pools: AUROC 0.47-0.56, so no strong drift confound for baselines
